title: A handle grown at a knot sphere's line lets learning remove the dissonance the sphere forces
subject: What growing a Fano atom into a knot sphere at a line, and then learning, does to the sphere's forced dissonance
conclusion: Splicing a Fano atom at a line of a knot sphere makes a torus whose law extends with no even face, and if the grown law is its only unsatisfiable class, as computed on every grown torus from K_2 to K_5, learning at the dissonance with the state fixed then removes it. Every such removal changes a sign in the grown handle, so growth and learning together remove what neither removes alone.
